articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) today announced a significant expansion of its Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program, adding several new vehicles and charger options that give customers greater energy resilience and choice in how they power their lives and participate in California's clean energy future. This includes the addition of Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex as approved partners, broadening the network of automakers, charger manufacturers, and software solutions providers participating in the program. Q: What is PGE announcing? A: Today, PGE announced a major expansion of its Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program, adding new vehicles and charger options through partnerships with Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex. This expanded network of automakers, chargers, and software solutions gives customers more choices, including the addition of Kia, Volvo, Polestar, and Nissan EVs . articles.summary: Dozens of restaurants and commercial caterers across Central and Northern California will soon be set to cook up new plans for growth with grants from the California Restaurant Foundation and The PGE Corporation Foundation. The two foundations have partnered to give $5,000 grants to 239 restaurants in 30 counties across PGE's service area. The charitable contributions will total $1.4 million. Both the number of grant recipients and the total dollar amount are records for the partnership since it began in 2021. "Local restaurants are vital to our communities," said Carla Peterman, Executive Vice President, Corporate Affairs, PGE Corporation, and Chair of the Board, The PGE Corporation Foundation. "They serve as economic engines, gathering hubs and cultural anchors. They support local and regional farms and other food producers and small businesses. articles.title: Keeping Restaurants Cooking: Nearly 240 Restaurants Receive Resilience Grants Funded by The PG&E Corporation Foundation

articles.summary: Most every day, somewhere in Pacific Gas and Electric's (PGE) service area in Northern and Central California, an underground utility line is damaged due to digging. Each of these incidents pose a public safety risk requiring a 911 response and can result in repair bills averaging $3,500. To help prevent these incidents and to raise awareness of the importance of calling 811 before any digging project, large or small, Tuesday, August 11 is recognized as National 811 Day. Not contacting 811 before digging is the top driver of damages to buried utilities every year. In PGE's service area alone, there were over 1,200 line strikes during 2025, and in 55% of these incidents, 811 was not called. Underground utility lines can be shallow, sometimes only a few inches below the surface, so it is important to call 811 before any project that involves digging, even for seemingly small projects like building or replacing a fence, planting and landscaping. articles.title: National 811 Day: Damaging Underground Utility Lines During Digging Can be a Serious Public Safety Issue
